editorial:
Imagine being stuck in a boring office job and a messy home life when a ghost from your past suddenly shows up. That is exactly what happens to Kosuke, a stiff accountant who gets a surprise visit from his childhood buddy, Shozo. The catch is that Shozo is dying and wants to go on one last wild adventure. He convinces Kosuke to help him hunt for a rare black carp fish in Nagano that could be worth a mountain of money. It starts off as a weird get-rich-quick scheme, but it quickly turns into a heartfelt road trip about two guys trying to make peace with their lives before time runs out.

You will love how the chemistry between the two leads feels real, moving from annoying arguments to deep bonding. The pacing is slow and steady, which helps you feel the weight of their friendship. While the plot is simple, the emotional payoff is huge. If you enjoy stories about second chances, you should definitely track this down. You can try renting it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you are a fan of classic Japanese cinema, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the end, the quest for the expensive fish becomes less important than the bond between the friends. Shozo passes away, but he dies knowing he reconnected with Kosuke. The movie wraps up by showing that the real treasure was not the money from the carp, but the forgiveness and closure they found together. Kosuke is left changed, feeling more alive and less trapped by his boring routine after saying a proper goodbye.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves touching stories about old friends and life lessons.
